Export a Fitted Model, Survival Matrix, or Data Dictionary to Python

Source: R/python_export.R
export_to_python.Rd

Writes a fitted TempleCBE model (or a data frame / survival matrix / data dictionary) to a directory of plain files a Python session can read with no R runtime: CSV tables, a JSON manifest and model metadata, and a small Python loader script (`<name>_load.py`) that reads them back with the standard library, or with `pandas` when it is installed. This is the package function behind README gap area 4 ("Python & Reticulate Cross-Language ML"): before it, the only Python-facing exports were [find_python()] (a locator for the PDF converter), `adapter_tidymodels_survex()` and the DALEX summarizers, and the reticulate vignette showed only raw user code calling Python from R.

Usage

export_to_python(
  object,
  path,
  name = "templecbe_export",
  eval_time = NULL,
  new_data = NULL,
  penalty = NULL,
  dictionary = NULL,
  format = c("files", "pickle"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'python_export'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

The object to export: a data frame, a matrix, a `coxnet_model`, a `cv_coxnet`, a `joint_model`, or a named list.

path

Directory the export is written to. Created if needed.

name

File-name stem for the artifacts (default `"templecbe_export"`). Must be a single string without a path separator.

eval_time, new_data

Passed to [predict()] for `coxnet_model` / `cv_coxnet` / `joint_model` objects to also export a survival matrix. Both must be given together; otherwise no survival matrix is written. `eval_time` must be finite, non-negative, sorted and free of duplicates.

penalty

Penalty passed to [generics::tidy()] / [predict()] for `coxnet_model` objects. Defaults to the model's own penalty.

dictionary

Optional data frame (a column dictionary) to export alongside `object`, as `dictionary.csv` and `dictionary.json`.

format

`"files"` (default) or `"pickle"` (additionally save a `reticulate` pickle; see the Reticulate pickle format section).

overwrite

If `FALSE` (default), refuse to write into a directory that already holds an export with the same `name`.

x

The object to print (the result of the function).

...

Not used.

Value

Invisibly, a list of class `python_export` with `path`, `name`, `object_class`, `format` and the `files` written (absolute paths).

What is exported

* A data frame or matrix: `<name>_data.csv`. * A `coxnet_model` ([coxnet()]): `coefficients.csv` (the [generics::tidy()] coefficients at `penalty`), `model.json` (penalty, mixture, predictor names, outcome type), and, when `new_data` and `eval_time` are given, `survival.csv` (one row per subject, one column per evaluation time). * A `cv_coxnet` object: coefficients at `"lambda.min"`, `metrics.csv` (the cross-validated metrics, when present), and `model.json`. * A `joint_model`: the [generics::tidy()] coefficients and `model.json` (component model classes); a survival matrix is added when `new_data` and `eval_time` are given, from the `.pred_survival` list-column of [predict.joint_model()]. * A named list: each data-frame element as `<name>_<element>.csv` and the whole list as `<name>.json`. * A data dictionary passed as `dictionary` (a data frame, for example the `matched` table of [reconcile_column_dictionary()]): `dictionary.csv` and `dictionary.json`.

Every export also writes `manifest.json` (package and R versions, object class, file list, creation time) and `<name>_load.py`. The loader exposes `load_coefficients()`, `load_survival()`, `load_dictionary()` and `load_manifest()`, each returning `pandas` DataFrames when `pandas` is importable and plain lists of dicts otherwise, and `load_data()` only when a data file was actually exported (a data frame or matrix object): model exports write no `<name>_data.csv`, so their loaders do not define it instead of raising `FileNotFoundError`.

Reticulate pickle format

With `format = "pickle"`, the same payload is additionally saved as `<name>.pkl` with [reticulate::py_save_object()], which needs the reticulate package (a `Suggests` dependency, not installed everywhere). The plain files are always written, so a pickle failure never loses the export; when `reticulate` is absent the function stops with a clear message instead of writing a partial pickle. A pickle is Python-version sensitive and opaque to other tools, so prefer the default `"files"` format for artifacts that must be inspected, versioned, or read outside Python.

See also

[find_python()], [reconcile_column_dictionary()], [adapter_tidymodels_survex()]

Examples

# \donttest{
out <- export_to_python(head(mtcars), path = tempfile("pyexp_"), name = "demo")
out$files
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmpMhtxuZ/pyexp_22e65229ad0/demo_data.csv"     
#> [2] "/tmp/RtmpMhtxuZ/pyexp_22e65229ad0/demo_load.py"      
#> [3] "/tmp/RtmpMhtxuZ/pyexp_22e65229ad0/demo_manifest.json"
# The loader is plain Python; read it back without reticulate:
cat(readLines(file.path(out$path, "demo_load.py")), sep = "\n")
#> """Loader for the TempleCBE Python export "demo".
#> 
#> Reads the CSV/JSON artifacts written by TempleCBE::export_to_python()
#> from the directory this file lives in. pandas is used when available;
#> otherwise each loader returns a plain list of dicts.
